pathway.title: TripAdvisor, Inc. — Credit Snapshot
pathway.question: Should we own this issuer, in which instrument, and why?

runs.text: Tripadvisor's earnings fell sharply in 2026. Adjusted EBITDA was USD 71.1 million in Q3 2026 against USD 107.8 million a year earlier, and USD 163.9 million over nine months against USD 251.3 million, so LTM Adjusted EBITDA is USD 207.3 million against USD 294.7 million for FY2025 on revenue of USD 1,559.1 million over the LTM period [CP-1]. The decline is concentrated in Hotels and Other, whose revenue fell 23% in Q3 2026 and which took a goodwill impairment of USD 369.5 million. Hotels and Other still produced USD 143.6 million of the USD 207.3 million LTM Adjusted EBITDA, at a margin of 23.0%, while Experiences produced USD 63.7 million at a margin of 6.8% [CP-1]. The business therefore leans on the segment management expects to keep being hurt by search changes, which is the most important fact for the credit.

Tripadvisor's debt is simple: one Term Loan B of USD 833.9 million due July 8, 2031, no financial covenant on that loan, and an undrawn USD 500.0 million revolver due June 29, 2028, after the USD 345.0 million convertible notes were repaid from cash on April 1, 2026 [CP-1]. Gross debt to LTM Adjusted EBITDA is 4.02x, the same as at year end 2025 because debt and earnings fell by similar proportions; net of cash it is 0.61x, but net of the operator payables that sit against the cash it is 2.53x, and after deducting stock-based compensation the gross ratio is 6.08x [CP-1]. LTM interest cover on cash interest is 3.50x, down from 4.99x for FY2025 [CP-1]. The revolver carries a maximum total net leverage covenant whose reported ratio is not printed, so headroom cannot be measured [CP-1].

Tripadvisor's liquidity is large but seasonal. Cash of USD 706.8 million and an undrawn revolver of USD 497.7 million give USD 1,204.5 million, or USD 807.7 million after deducting deferred merchant payables of USD 396.8 million owed to experience operators [CP-1]. Operating cash flow was negative USD 122.0 million in Q3 2026, LTM operating cash flow is USD 27.4 million, and LTM free cash flow is negative USD 17.5 million, because experience bookings bring cash in during the first half and reverse in the second half [CP-1, CP-1A]. Scheduled term loan amortisation is only USD 8.5 million a year, with USD 797.8 million due in 2031 [CP-1].

Tripadvisor completed the sale of TheFork to American Express on November 1, 2026 for about USD 741.0 million of net cash against a USD 700.0 million headline price, with an expected fourth-quarter gain of about USD 487.0 million. Management says it currently expects to prioritise reduction of long-term debt, but that is a stated intent, not an executed commitment, and whether the term loan can be prepaid from proceeds depends on a credit agreement that is not supplied [CP-1A]. On an illustrative basis, before seasonal outflow and restructuring cost, cash plus the proceeds would exceed the term loan by USD 613.9 million, which shows the size of the effect rather than a forecast [CP-1].

Tripadvisor has no controlling stockholder since the April 2025 merger with LTRIP and no sponsor, paid no dividends, bought back no shares in 2026 and repaid the notes from cash, which supports a creditor-friendly reading of behaviour; a cooperation agreement dated March 22, 2026 and USD 3.3 million of activism costs show outside pressure on strategy, and a restructuring plan for Hotels and Other began on November 4, 2026 [CP-1A]. No priming, uptiering or collateral release is documented, but the pack cannot show them either way because the credit agreement is missing [CP-1A].

cells.text: After TheFork became a discontinued operation, continuing operations have two reportable segments: Experiences (Viator, Tripadvisor and third-party points of sale) and Hotels and Other (hotel metasearch and restaurant guidance, advertising, Cruise Critic).
Two businesses with opposite trajectories sit under one capital structure, so debt is serviced by the declining segment while the growing segment is built out.

Revenue is "generated primarily through commission-based transactions on completed experiences offerings"; the traveler pays up front, the commission is deferred revenue and the operator share is a deferred merchant payable until completion.
Cash arrives before operators are paid, so reported cash includes operator money and swings with booking seasonality.

Revenue "is generated primarily through click-based advertising including cost-per-click"; media advertising is impression-based. Q3 2026 revenue was Hotels 109.7, Media and advertising 27.7 and Other 14.2.
Pricing and volume depend on advertiser demand and on traffic the company does not control, which makes this revenue less contractually visible than commissions.
More than 425,000 bookable experiences from 70,000 operators on a shared supply platform, as stated by the company.
A company-stated scale metric; it supports marketplace breadth but is not audited and carries no margin information.

Experience bookings were approximately 6.8 million in Q3 2026 (up about 2%) and 18.9 million over nine months (up about 6%); gross booking value was $1.3 billion in Q3 2026 (about flat) and $3.9 billion over nine months (up about 5%).
Bookings rose while Q3 revenue fell 3%, so revenue per booking is falling; the filing cites lower average booking values and higher cancellations.
In FY2025 Experiences was "approximately 55% of the Company's total revenue from continuing operations and 30% of our adjusted EBITDA from continuing operations".
Most earnings still came from Hotels and Other in FY2025; the LTM figure in the financial handoff puts that share near 69%.

"Google, a partner and significant source of traffic to our platform, frequently promotes its own competing products in its search results"; management expects Hotels and Other to continue to be impacted, including by AI overviews displacing top-ranked links.
The main earnings segment depends on a supplier of traffic that also competes; a ranking change can cut revenue without any change in demand, and paid replacement traffic lifts marketing cost.

Booking (10% or more of consolidated revenue) together with Expedia accounted for approximately 21% and 22% of consolidated revenue in FY2025 and FY2024, "with nearly all of this revenue recorded within our Hotels and Other segment".
Two advertisers hold a large share of the shrinking segment's revenue; a reduction by either would fall disproportionately on Adjusted EBITDA.
Marketing was the largest cost at 48.8% of revenue in Q3 2026, against personnel at 21.5% of revenue (94.0 over 436.4, calculated); personnel cost fell 24% year on year.
Q3 PR page:1 and page:2; Q3 10-Q page:2.
A marketing-heavy, largely variable cost base can be cut with revenue, but personnel cuts are the main fixed-cost lever and carry restructuring cash costs.
Capital expenditures were 31.8 for nine months 2026 against 48.2 a year earlier, including capitalized website development.
Capital-light: spending can be flexed down, so free cash flow is driven by operating cash flow and working capital rather than capex.

Performance is highest in the second and third quarters; in the second half "particularly in the third quarter" cash flows from experience bookings are typically negative; a "Reserve Now, Pay Later" option lets travelers defer payment until two days before the experience.
The second-half outflow and a growing pay-later share both reduce float; usable liquidity is lower than the cash balance in the weakest cash quarters.

From late February 2026 the Middle East conflict, flooding in Hawaii, civil unrest in Mexico and weather events in Europe and the U.S. reduced bookings, gross booking value and revenue and raised cancellation rates in Experiences; management expects tensions to affect the fourth quarter.
Management attributes the slowdown to external events; the filing does not quantify the share due to events versus the Tripadvisor search headwind, so the cause is not separable.

The November 2025 plan targeted "at least $85 million in annualized gross cost savings"; headcount was approximately 2,590 at December 31, 2025 and approximately 2,455 at September 30, 2026, of which approximately 870 were TheFork employees.
Savings are a management expectation and only partly visible in the 24% drop in Q3 2026 personnel cost; they offset, but do not remove, the revenue decline.
Not disclosed: the experiences commission rate, repeat-customer share and operator concentration are not in the pack.
Searched the 10-K and the Q3 10-Q for take rate, commission rate and retention wording.
Margin resilience of Experiences cannot be tested on price; only volume and revenue trends are available.

runs.text: Strengths. Tripadvisor has liquidity of USD 1,204.5 million against debt of USD 833.9 million and no financial covenant on the term loan, which removes near-term refinancing and covenant pressure; this is a Documentary Fact [CP-1]. Its capital structure is a single term loan due 2031 with amortisation of USD 8.5 million a year, after the convertible notes were repaid in cash, which keeps debt service predictable apart from the floating rate; this is a Documentary Fact [CP-1, CP-1A]. The TheFork sale added about USD 741.0 million of net cash on November 1, 2026, which creates the option to cut debt; the closing is a Documentary Fact and the debt-reduction intent is Management Language, qualified as not a commitment [CP-1A]. Experiences volumes are still growing, with bookings up about 6% and gross booking value up about 5% over nine months 2026, which supports the replacement thesis even though Experiences revenue fell 3% in Q3 2026; this is a Documentary Fact with an Analyst Interpretation on what it means [CP-1A]. Capital spending of USD 31.8 million over nine months 2026 is light relative to revenue and can be flexed, so free cash flow is driven by operating cash flow; this is an Analyst Interpretation of Documentary Facts [CP-1, CP-1A]. There is no controlling stockholder or sponsor, no dividends, and no buybacks in 2026, which limits value leakage; this is an Analyst Interpretation of documented actions [CP-1A].

Weaknesses. Tripadvisor's earnings are falling and concentrated: LTM Adjusted EBITDA of USD 207.3 million is down from USD 294.7 million for FY2025, with about 69% from Hotels and Other, a segment with a goodwill impairment of USD 369.5 million and a margin that Experiences, at 6.8%, does not yet replace; this is a Documentary Fact [CP-1]. The segment that earns most depends on search traffic from a partner that also competes, and Booking and Expedia together were about 21% of FY2025 consolidated revenue, so a ranking or advertiser change can cut earnings quickly; the facts are Documentary and the mechanism is an Analyst Interpretation [CP-1A]. Cash conversion is weak: LTM free cash flow is negative USD 17.5 million and reported cash is matched by USD 396.8 million of deferred merchant payables, so usable liquidity is lower than the headline; this is a Documentary Fact [CP-1]. Leverage looks lower than it is because Adjusted EBITDA adds back stock-based compensation: gross leverage is 4.02x on Adjusted EBITDA and 6.08x after stock-based compensation, and cash interest cover falls from 3.50x to 2.32x; this is an Analyst Interpretation of CP-1 figures [CP-1]. The term loan rate floats and the 10-K says it is not hedged, so a rate rise reduces cover while earnings fall; this is a Documentary Fact [CP-1]. Governance depends on a board facing activism with no anchor holder, so portfolio actions that affect lenders are plausible and the credit agreement protections are unknown; this is an Analyst Interpretation [CP-1A]. The synthesis cannot test creditor protections, covenant headroom or post-sale net debt from the supplied sources; this is Insufficient Information and is not treated as adverse.

blocks.title: Transaction summary and new debt issues

runs.text: The one transaction in the period is the sale of TheFork, the company's European online restaurant reservation and management platform, to American Express Travel Related Services Company, Inc. (a strategic buyer; no sponsor is involved). On June 14, 2026 the company entered into a put option agreement to sell the legal entities comprising TheFork "for $700.0 million in cash, subject to certain adjustments", and the Q3 10-Q states that American Express "provided an irrevocable commitment to acquire TheFork" (Q3 10-Q page:11). After the French Works Council consultation completed on July 30, 2026, the company exercised the put on August 1, 2026 and signed the Equity Purchase Agreement on August 2, 2026. The sale closed on November 1, 2026; the Q3 10-Q states "The total net cash consideration received at closing was approximately $741.0 million", reflecting adjustments for closing working capital, cash and indebtedness and net of transaction expenses; management expects a fourth-quarter 2026 gain of approximately $487.0 million and transaction costs of $16.0 million to $18.0 million netted against the gain, and warns that both amounts "may differ materially" (Q3 10-Q page:11 and page:65). Status: closed, with final adjustments still open. Accounting: TheFork was classified as held for sale and as a discontinued operation from the second quarter of 2026, with assets held for sale of 290.7 and liabilities held for sale of 62.3 at September 30, 2026 (Q3 10-Q page:12 and page:16), and an accumulated other comprehensive loss of 21.4 to be netted against the gain (page:17). A Transition Services Agreement of up to 12 months, for finance, information technology, human resources and other administrative services, started at closing (page:12-13), and the company expects no significant effect on future operating cash flows (page:65). Liquidity effect: the proceeds arrived after the September 30, 2026 balance sheet and are in no reported cash figure; management states that the proceeds provide "additional flexibility in its capital structure", that it "will continue to maintain optionality with respect to its use of the net proceeds", and that it "currently expects that the Company will prioritize reduction of its long-term debt" (Q3 10-Q page:65). That is a Management Language statement of intent, not an executed commitment, and the pack does not show whether the Term Loan B can be prepaid with sale proceeds or whether the credit agreement requires any mandatory prepayment from asset sales, because the credit agreement is not supplied. Credit effect, analyst reading: the sale removes a segment that contributed 221 of FY2025 consolidated revenue (10-K page:189) and, with it, diversification away from advertising, but it leaves the capital structure unchanged until proceeds are applied, and it adds to cash against a term loan of 833.9.

New debt issues: none in 2026. The company raised no new debt in the first nine months of 2026; the only debt movement was the April 1, 2026 repayment of the 0.25% Convertible 2026 Senior Notes at maturity for $345.4 million including interest, funded by cash on hand, after which the capped calls expired unexercised (Q3 10-Q page:25-26). Earlier issues that define the present structure: the $500 million Term Loan B Facility issued July 8, 2024 at 99.75% of par, used to redeem the $500 million 2025 Senior Notes on July 15, 2024; the $350 million tack-on of March 20, 2025 at 98.56% of par, also due July 8, 2031 at SOFR plus 2.75%; and the Third Amendment of June 5, 2025, which redefined the revolver's springing maturity by reference to the 2026 notes and a cash test (10-K page:91 and page:160-163). Analyst reading: because the condition refers to notes outstanding of $200 million or more, it appears moot now that the notes are repaid, but the amended text itself is not in the pack. The revolver of $500.0 million matures June 29, 2028 and is undrawn.

Other transactions in the history that bear on the creditor: the merger with LTRIP, which closed on April 29, 2025 at an aggregate transaction price of $437 million, accounted for as a repurchase of the company's own shares held by LTRIP; before it, on March 20, 2025, the company lent LTRIP $326.7 million (about $327 million) so LTRIP could settle its exchangeable debentures, and that loan balance was folded into the transaction price (Q3 10-Q page:10; 10-K page:72). The aggregate cash paid including expenses was $410.7 million, plus 3,037,959 shares valued at about $38.9 million, less $13.1 million of LTRIP tax losses retained (Q3 10-Q page:10). The sources state that the tack-on proceeds were used to repay the 2026 notes; they do not state that the tack-on funded the merger. As an analyst reading only, gross debt rose by about 341 during 2025 while about 450.7 left the company in the merger repurchase and share buyback, and the notes were then repaid from cash in 2026; the filings do not link the two flows. A further restructuring plan was initiated on November 4, 2026 for the Hotels and Other segment with expected pre-tax costs of approximately $15 million to $20 million (Q3 10-Q page:37), and the Q3 release adds that management expects annualized gross savings of approximately $40 million (Q3 PR page:3), a release-only management claim that does not appear in the 10-Q.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: TripAdvisor, Inc. enters the fourth quarter of 2026 with a lower-earning but lower-debt capital structure than a year ago. On the continuing-operations perimeter, LTM Adjusted EBITDA is 207.3 against 294.7 for FY2025, driven by Hotels and Other, whose revenue fell 23% in Q3 2026, while Experiences revenue fell 3% in the same quarter after growing earlier in the year. Debt principal has fallen from 1,185 at December 31, 2025 to 833.9 at September 30, 2026 because the 345.0 convertible notes were repaid in cash on April 1, 2026, so gross debt to LTM Adjusted EBITDA is 4.02x, the same as at year end 2025 only because EBITDA and debt fell together. Net of 706.8 of cash the ratio is 0.61x, but 396.8 of deferred merchant payables, amounts owed to experience operators after travel, sit against that cash, and on a cash-less-float basis net leverage is 2.53x. Free cash flow is negative on an LTM basis, interest cover on cash interest is 3.50x LTM, and the term loan has no financial covenant while the revolver carries a leverage maximum whose reported level is not printed in the 2026 filings. The TheFork sale added about 741.0 of net cash on November 1, 2026, after the balance sheet date, so the reported figures understate the post-sale cash position. Every ratio below rests on management Adjusted EBITDA, which adds back stock-based compensation, so the ratios are better read as a ceiling on earnings capacity than as a covenant calculation.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Hotels and Other revenue fell 23% in Q3 2026 and 21% over nine months, and its Adjusted EBITDA fell 41% in Q3 2026 against Q3 2025 (Q3 PR page:1 and page:14). Management attributes the decline to "the sustained acceleration of traffic acquisition headwinds negatively impacting this business due to the changes in the search landscape" (Q3 10-Q page:22), which reads as a structural rather than cyclical explanation (analyst reading). Experiences revenue fell 3% in Q3 2026 after growing 1% over nine months, with Adjusted EBITDA down 27% in Q3 2026; the 10-Q cites macro events, cancellations and search headwinds on the Tripadvisor point of sale (Q3 10-Q page:43 and page:49). Mechanism: the segment that supplies about 69% of LTM Adjusted EBITDA is the one in structural decline, and the growth segment's LTM margin is 6.8% against 23.0% for Hotels and Other, so group margin falls as mix shifts even before any further decline in Hotels and Other. Credit implication: debt capacity depends on how fast Hotels and Other earnings erode against how fast Experiences margin can expand; the November 4, 2026 restructuring plan (costs of approximately $15 million to $20 million, Q3 10-Q page:37) targets the cost base but management's claimed savings are a release-only statement (Q3 PR page:3) and are not carried here.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Adjusted EBITDA is defined in Q3 10-Q page:33 as net income from continuing operations plus taxes, other income and expense, depreciation and amortization, stock-based compensation, impairments, legal reserves and settlements, restructuring, transaction expenses and non-recurring items. Reported-basis bridge for nine months 2026, recomputed from printed lines: operating income of -321.6 plus depreciation and amortization of 56.5 plus the goodwill impairment of 369.5 gives 104.4; adding stock-based compensation 50.5, restructuring 7.8, legal reserves and other 1.9, transaction expenses 4.1 and deducting the 4.8 fraud recovery gives 163.9, which equals the reported figure (Q3 PR page:12-13; Q3 10-Q page:34-37). The Q3 2026 bridge is 51.7 plus 15.3, 0.9, 2.6 and 0.6 giving 71.1. Largest definitional sensitivity: stock-based compensation is an add-back of 70.2 over the LTM, so EBITDA after stock-based compensation is 137.1 and gross leverage on that basis is 6.08x. The Term Loan B has no financial covenant; the revolver covenant definition of total net leverage is not supplied, so none of the ratios here is the covenant ratio.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Tripadvisor, Inc. is in the middle of a deliberate change of business mix, and the creditor question is whether the new mix earns enough to carry the debt before the old mix erodes further. The old core, Hotels and Other, earns click-based and media advertising from travel partners and depends on traffic from search engines; management itself says search placement changes and AI overviews are reducing that traffic and that the segment will keep being affected. The new core, Experiences, is a commission-based marketplace for tours and activities led by Viator, which grew through 2025 but turned negative in the third quarter of 2026 after macro disruptions, higher cancellations and weaker Tripadvisor point-of-sale traffic. Against that, the company repaid its convertible notes in cash in April 2026, sold TheFork to American Express with closing on November 1, 2026 for about 741.0 of net cash, and started a further restructuring plan on November 4, 2026. Ownership changed in April 2025 when the merger with LTRIP removed the controlling stockholder, so there is no sponsor and no documented extraction by an owner, but also no anchor holder, and a cooperation agreement of March 22, 2026 and shareholder activism costs show outside pressure on strategy. What cannot be assessed from the pack is legal capacity: the credit agreement, the sale agreements and the beneficial ownership table are not supplied, so restrictions on asset sales, prepayment of sale proceeds and investor control are known only from filing summaries. The financial scale of these points is in the financial handoff: LTM Adjusted EBITDA of 207.3, debt principal of 833.9 and cash of 706.8 before the sale proceeds.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The one transaction in the period is the sale of TheFork, the company's European online restaurant reservation and management platform, to American Express Travel Related Services Company, Inc. (a strategic buyer; no sponsor is involved). On June 14, 2026 the company entered into a put option agreement to sell the legal entities comprising TheFork "for $700.0 million in cash, subject to certain adjustments", and the Q3 10-Q states that American Express "provided an irrevocable commitment to acquire TheFork" (Q3 10-Q page:11). After the French Works Council consultation completed on July 30, 2026, the company exercised the put on August 1, 2026 and signed the Equity Purchase Agreement on August 2, 2026. The sale closed on November 1, 2026; the Q3 10-Q states "The total net cash consideration received at closing was approximately $741.0 million", reflecting adjustments for closing working capital, cash and indebtedness and net of transaction expenses; management expects a fourth-quarter 2026 gain of approximately $487.0 million and transaction costs of $16.0 million to $18.0 million netted against the gain, and warns that both amounts "may differ materially" (Q3 10-Q page:11 and page:65). Status: closed, with final adjustments still open. Accounting: TheFork was classified as held for sale and as a discontinued operation from the second quarter of 2026, with assets held for sale of 290.7 and liabilities held for sale of 62.3 at September 30, 2026 (Q3 10-Q page:12 and page:16), and an accumulated other comprehensive loss of 21.4 to be netted against the gain (page:17). A Transition Services Agreement of up to 12 months, for finance, information technology, human resources and other administrative services, started at closing (page:12-13), and the company expects no significant effect on future operating cash flows (page:65). Liquidity effect: the proceeds arrived after the September 30, 2026 balance sheet and are in no reported cash figure; management states that the proceeds provide "additional flexibility in its capital structure", that it "will continue to maintain optionality with respect to its use of the net proceeds", and that it "currently expects that the Company will prioritize reduction of its long-term debt" (Q3 10-Q page:65). That is a Management Language statement of intent, not an executed commitment, and the pack does not show whether the Term Loan B can be prepaid with sale proceeds or whether the credit agreement requires any mandatory prepayment from asset sales, because the credit agreement is not supplied. Credit effect, analyst reading: the sale removes a segment that contributed 221 of FY2025 consolidated revenue (10-K page:189) and, with it, diversification away from advertising, but it leaves the capital structure unchanged until proceeds are applied, and it adds to cash against a term loan of 833.9.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: New debt issues: none in 2026. The company raised no new debt in the first nine months of 2026; the only debt movement was the April 1, 2026 repayment of the 0.25% Convertible 2026 Senior Notes at maturity for $345.4 million including interest, funded by cash on hand, after which the capped calls expired unexercised (Q3 10-Q page:25-26). Earlier issues that define the present structure: the $500 million Term Loan B Facility issued July 8, 2024 at 99.75% of par, used to redeem the $500 million 2025 Senior Notes on July 15, 2024; the $350 million tack-on of March 20, 2025 at 98.56% of par, also due July 8, 2031 at SOFR plus 2.75%; and the Third Amendment of June 5, 2025, which redefined the revolver's springing maturity by reference to the 2026 notes and a cash test (10-K page:91 and page:160-163). Analyst reading: because the condition refers to notes outstanding of $200 million or more, it appears moot now that the notes are repaid, but the amended text itself is not in the pack. fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Tripadvisor, Inc. is a moderately leveraged credit with ample near-term liquidity and no large maturity before 2031, but its earnings base is shrinking and the case rests on whether Experiences can replace Hotels and Other earnings. The strongest support is liquidity of USD 1,204.5 million (cash of USD 706.8 million plus an undrawn USD 497.7 million revolver), a single term loan of USD 833.9 million with no financial covenant, and about USD 741.0 million of new sale proceeds. The weakest point is falling earnings: LTM Adjusted EBITDA of USD 207.3 million compares with USD 294.7 million in FY2025, and Hotels and Other supplies about 69% of it. What decides the outcome is how quickly that segment erodes and whether the sale proceeds reduce debt.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Tripadvisor's earnings fell sharply in 2026. Adjusted EBITDA was USD 71.1 million in Q3 2026 against USD 107.8 million a year earlier, and USD 163.9 million over nine months against USD 251.3 million, so LTM Adjusted EBITDA is USD 207.3 million against USD 294.7 million for FY2025 on revenue of USD 1,559.1 million over the LTM period [CP-1]. The decline is concentrated in Hotels and Other, whose revenue fell 23% in Q3 2026 and which took a goodwill impairment of USD 369.5 million. Hotels and Other still produced USD 143.6 million of the USD 207.3 million LTM Adjusted EBITDA, at a margin of 23.0%, while Experiences produced USD 63.7 million at a margin of 6.8% [CP-1]. The business therefore leans on the segment management expects to keep being hurt by search changes, which is the most important fact for the credit.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Tripadvisor's debt is simple: one Term Loan B of USD 833.9 million due July 8, 2031, no financial covenant on that loan, and an undrawn USD 500.0 million revolver due June 29, 2028, after the USD 345.0 million convertible notes were repaid from cash on April 1, 2026 [CP-1]. Gross debt to LTM Adjusted EBITDA is 4.02x, the same as at year end 2025 because debt and earnings fell by similar proportions; net of cash it is 0.61x, but net of the operator payables that sit against the cash it is 2.53x, and after deducting stock-based compensation the gross ratio is 6.08x [CP-1]. LTM interest cover on cash interest is 3.50x, down from 4.99x for FY2025 [CP-1]. The revolver carries a maximum total net leverage covenant whose reported ratio is not printed, so headroom cannot be measured [CP-1].

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Tripadvisor's liquidity is large but seasonal. Cash of USD 706.8 million and an undrawn revolver of USD 497.7 million give USD 1,204.5 million, or USD 807.7 million after deducting deferred merchant payables of USD 396.8 million owed to experience operators [CP-1]. Operating cash flow was negative USD 122.0 million in Q3 2026, LTM operating cash flow is USD 27.4 million, and LTM free cash flow is negative USD 17.5 million, because experience bookings bring cash in during the first half and reverse in the second half [CP-1, CP-1A]. Scheduled term loan amortisation is only USD 8.5 million a year, with USD 797.8 million due in 2031 [CP-1].

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Tripadvisor completed the sale of TheFork to American Express on November 1, 2026 for about USD 741.0 million of net cash against a USD 700.0 million headline price, with an expected fourth-quarter gain of about USD 487.0 million. Management says it currently expects to prioritise reduction of long-term debt, but that is a stated intent, not an executed commitment, and whether the term loan can be prepaid from proceeds depends on a credit agreement that is not supplied [CP-1A]. On an illustrative basis, before seasonal outflow and restructuring cost, cash plus the proceeds would exceed the term loan by USD 613.9 million, which shows the size of the effect rather than a forecast [CP-1].

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Tripadvisor has no controlling stockholder since the April 2025 merger with LTRIP and no sponsor, paid no dividends, bought back no shares in 2026 and repaid the notes from cash, which supports a creditor-friendly reading of behaviour; a cooperation agreement dated March 22, 2026 and USD 3.3 million of activism costs show outside pressure on strategy, and a restructuring plan for Hotels and Other began on November 4, 2026 [CP-1A]. No priming, uptiering or collateral release is documented, but the pack cannot show them either way because the credit agreement is missing [CP-1A].

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Strengths. Tripadvisor has liquidity of USD 1,204.5 million against debt of USD 833.9 million and no financial covenant on the term loan, which removes near-term refinancing and covenant pressure; this is a Documentary Fact [CP-1]. Its capital structure is a single term loan due 2031 with amortisation of USD 8.5 million a year, after the convertible notes were repaid in cash, which keeps debt service predictable apart from the floating rate; this is a Documentary Fact [CP-1, CP-1A]. The TheFork sale added about USD 741.0 million of net cash on November 1, 2026, which creates the option to cut debt; the closing is a Documentary Fact and the debt-reduction intent is Management Language, qualified as not a commitment [CP-1A]. Experiences volumes are still growing, with bookings up about 6% and gross booking value up about 5% over nine months 2026, which supports the replacement thesis even though Experiences revenue fell 3% in Q3 2026; this is a Documentary Fact with an Analyst Interpretation on what it means [CP-1A]. Capital spending of USD 31.8 million over nine months 2026 is light relative to revenue and can be flexed, so free cash flow is driven by operating cash flow; this is an Analyst Interpretation of Documentary Facts [CP-1, CP-1A]. There is no controlling stockholder or sponsor, no dividends, and no buybacks in 2026, which limits value leakage; this is an Analyst Interpretation of documented actions [CP-1A].

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Weaknesses. Tripadvisor's earnings are falling and concentrated: LTM Adjusted EBITDA of USD 207.3 million is down from USD 294.7 million for FY2025, with about 69% from Hotels and Other, a segment with a goodwill impairment of USD 369.5 million and a margin that Experiences, at 6.8%, does not yet replace; this is a Documentary Fact [CP-1]. The segment that earns most depends on search traffic from a partner that also competes, and Booking and Expedia together were about 21% of FY2025 consolidated revenue, so a ranking or advertiser change can cut earnings quickly; the facts are Documentary and the mechanism is an Analyst Interpretation [CP-1A]. Cash conversion is weak: LTM free cash flow is negative USD 17.5 million and reported cash is matched by USD 396.8 million of deferred merchant payables, so usable liquidity is lower than the headline; this is a Documentary Fact [CP-1]. Leverage looks lower than it is because Adjusted EBITDA adds back stock-based compensation: gross leverage is 4.02x on Adjusted EBITDA and 6.08x after stock-based compensation, and cash interest cover falls from 3.50x to 2.32x; this is an Analyst Interpretation of CP-1 figures [CP-1]. The term loan rate floats and the 10-K says it is not hedged, so a rate rise reduces cover while earnings fall; this is a Documentary Fact [CP-1]. Governance depends on a board facing activism with no anchor holder, so portfolio actions that affect lenders are plausible and the credit agreement protections are unknown; this is an Analyst Interpretation [CP-1A]. The synthesis cannot test creditor protections, covenant headroom or post-sale net debt from the supplied sources; this is Insufficient Information and is not treated as adverse.
